title: Jazz clubs that paid jazz bands too little
summary: Societies with thousands of dues-paying members hire the veterans cheaply, paying $100 to him and $35 to sidemen at a packed concert.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, before you do that, don't you think we ought to talk a little bit more about those--that dry period, from '58 to say '73---
Well, it was just drive -- what the hell can you talk about---

Well, you felt that some of the places - some of the groups that called you to play for $50.00 and the side men would get $35.00 and they'd jam the place with 500 people -- you were a little bit angry about that.

Yes - well, I think they were taking advantage of the fact that our kind of music wasn't making it. But, it really was. It really was with them it was. And, they figured they could get us cheap because we weren't working that much.
And, how true they were. We were glad to get some of those jobs. And, I really have to - at this point - put down some of the jazz clubs -- some of these so-called jazz clubs.
Well, they were just getting started then - weren't they?

No -there was plenty of them around. There was plenty of them around and they have a big membership of 2,000 - some of them 3,000 - and they pay dues and they certainly could have paid more money for the good groups that I got together and got out there; I remember once going up to Connecticut, I got $100.00 and they all got $35.00 and at concert, they were hanging from the chandeliers. And, anytime that thing every happened, it's like my wife said -- anytime that happened, they did such tremendous business -- never did any of those guys ever say - you guys were wonderful today; we made a lot of money; here's an extra $20.00; never. That never happened. So, I think, you know, they were playing guys that

played our kind of music cheap. They were just trying to get us as cheap as they could, knowing that we were having a difficult time. So, anyway, about the end of this whole thing and I was getting pretty discouraged again -- was the fact that I had this wonderful job and -- at the top of the--- I forget what the heck---
